subject: Scheduling: technical deep-dive availability for multi-region architects
messages:
From: Alexei Popov <alexei@cloudmatrix.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finovate.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Technical deep-dive: Redwood runtime for low-latency inference

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The architecture team at CloudMatrix would like to run a 90-minute technical deep-dive focused on latency profiles, KV cache behavior across long-context flows, and routing/fallback policies. Attendees will be: myself (infra lead), Priya Singh (security architect), and two of our platform engineers.

We're distributed across SF (PST), London (GMT), and Bangalore (IST). Can you share 2–3 windows next week that would work for Redwood's SEs and engineering architect? Our main constraint is having both a Redwood solutions engineer and a Redwood architect on the call.

Preferred days: Tue/Wed/Thu. We are flexible with start times but would like an overlap that hits late morning London / early evening Bangalore if possible.

Thanks — Alexei

[Attachment: initial_requirements.docx (docx)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alexei Popov <alexei@cloudmatrix.io>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive: Redwood runtime for low-latency inference

Alexei —

Appreciate the context. Happy to run the 90-minute session. Sergio (solutions engineering lead) and Ben (runtime architect) are on copy. A couple quick notes before we lock times:

- We try to avoid late-night starts for our SEs but can rotate resources if necessary.
- One thing to watch: the recent Europe DST shift moved overlap windows slightly earlier for a couple of weeks; I included a quick heatmap (will attach) to show current local-times.

Proposed slots (all are duration 90m, times shown in each zone):
- Option A: Tue Nov 30 — 16:00 PST / 00:00 GMT (Wed) / 05:30 IST (Wed) — note this pushes London to midnight, so not ideal
- Option B: Wed Dec 1 — 07:00 PST / 15:00 GMT / 20:30 IST
- Option C: Wed Dec 1 — 10:00 PST / 18:00 GMT / 23:30 IST (late for Bangalore)

Can you confirm which of the above is least bad for your team? If none work, send 2 windows that work for you and we'll match availability. I'm attaching a quick availability heatmap and a tentative agenda.

Thanks,
Stephanie
--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
[Attachment: availability_heatmap_v1.png (png)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alexei Popov <alexei@cloudmatrix.io>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive: Redwood runtime for low-latency inference

Alexei / Stephanie —

I pulled the team's availability and sketched a heatmap. Quick callouts:

- Our preferred window to keep everyone sane is Option B (07:00 PST / 15:00 GMT / 20:30 IST). It hits mid-afternoon in EU and early night in APAC, which is better than pushing London to midnight.
- Ben will cover serving runtime internals and kernel selection; I'll cover routing, batching, and fallback behavior.
- If you want us to shift to an earlier EU time (14:00 GMT), we can do that but it would be 06:00 PST.

Attached: availability_heatmap_v1.png and a calendar invite draft (ICS).

Sergio

[Attachment: overlap_windows_v2.ics (calendar invite)]

Thanks — Option B looks closest. Small snag: our CTO's calendar just filled with an urgent vendor readout on Wed Dec 1 at 15:30 GMT, and Priya needs to be on both calls. Would it be possible to start 30 minutes earlier (14:30 GMT / 06:30 PST / 20:00 IST) so Priya can dial out at 15:30 GMT?

If Sergio/Ben can do 14:30 GMT start, we can lock it. Otherwise we may need to shift to Thu Dec 2.

Alexei
